title: Tensions Rise Over Strait of Hormuz as U.N. Faces Key Decision
description: The U.N. Security Council is set to vote on a Bahraini resolution aimed at protecting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal faces opposition from China and Russia, despite support from Gulf Arab states and the U.S. Amid rising oil prices and tensions, China's veto threatens consensus.

title: Bahrain's Security Council Challenge: Strait of Hormuz Resolution in Limbo
description: Bahrain, presiding over the UN Security Council, delayed a vote on a resolution intended to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This decision follows opposition from Russia and China, necessitating further negotiations. The resolution's aim is to ensure safe transit through the crucial passage, vital for global oil flow.

title: Iran names 5 ‘friendly nations’ free to use Strait of Hormuz - Russia and China included
description: The Kremlin has mocked the rest of the world by announcing that for Russia, 'Hormuz is open'.

title: Bahrain Waters Down UN Proposal On Opening Hormuz Strait By Force
description: Russia, China and France, all veto-wielding countries on the 15-member Security Council, had expressed opposition to approving the use of force.

title: Japan and Australia Strengthen Rare-Earth Elements Alliance
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans an Australia visit to discuss rare-earth element supply chains and safe Strait of Hormuz navigation. The visit follows Japan's rare-earths deal with France, amid efforts to reduce reliance on China's supply chain dominance. Discussions will also cover Indo-Pacific initiatives.

title: Crude oil ship heading to India diverted to China
description: Ping Shun, Iranian crude oil carrier, that had crossed the Strait of Hormuz and was signalling that it was heading to Vadinar, India, for the past three days is now signalling it is headed for China, as per marine logistics and commodity markets analytics firm Kpler.

title: UNSC to vote Saturday on Bahrain-led resolution on Strait of Hormuz
description: The UN Security Council will vote on a Bahrain-proposed resolution Saturday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, affirming open transit passage and authorizing "exclusively defensive measures" to secure navigation. This comes after earlier versions allowing the use of force faced opposition from China and Russia. The resolution aims to deter impediments to international navigation and establish a monitoring mechanism.

title: China, Europe and why Beijing took a swing at Iran over the Strait of Hormuz
description: Beijing takes a stand at the United Nations at the closure of shipping lanes.

title: China's covert political penetration of Taiwan raises alarm over systemic loopholes
description: China is increasingly using Taiwan's existing business, cultural, and exchange frameworks as a cover to quietly expand its political influence, according to a Taiwanese academic. These activities, he stated, are carefully disguised as routine interactions, making them harder to detect and counter, as reported by The Taipei Times.

title: Bahrain waters down UN proposal over opposition to allowing force to open Strait of Hormuz
description: UNITED NATIONS, Apr 3:  Bahrain has significantly watered down a proposed UN resolution on reopening the Strait of Hormuz amid opposition from China and Russia about allowing countries to use force to secure the critical waterway Iran has largely cut off to global shipping. The final draft of the proposal, obtained Thursday by The Associated Press, authorizes defensive – but not offensive – action to ensure vessels can safely transit the strait.
